    About this page

    An independent, mobile-friendly view of the AIP Congress 2026 program, built from the official Indico timetable (event 16926), retrieved 24 November 2026. Session and talk titles are as published; a few obvious typos were corrected.

    Times, rooms and abstracts can still change, so always confirm on the official pages close to the event.

    Tips

    Pick a day tab to focus, or All week for the full program. Search matches every word in any order, ignoring accents (e.g. dzurak silicon) — put “quotes” around words for an exact phrase; matches are highlighted. If a day has no matches, results from the rest of the week appear automatically. ClickTap a group badge (e.g. QST, NUPP) to filter to that group. Star individual talks or whole sessions, then open My agenda to see them in a list or calendar, export them, or share them as a link. Short forms of institutions work too (unsw, anu, usyd). Participants lists every speaker and convener by institution. During the congress, Now jumps to what is on.

    The page address keeps your day, search and filters, so you can bookmark or share a view. Once loaded, the page also works offline.

    Colour key

    Each stream takes its colour from a spectral line. The key, with every line drawn at its wavelength, is in , beside the Colour setting: Quiet keeps colour to thin lines, Vivid lets it fill each stream. ANZCOP is the 632.8 nm helium–neon laser; COMMAD a 455 nm InGaN blue LED; AIP groups hydrogen Hβ at 486.1 nm; Focus sessions the mercury e-line at 546.1 nm, the wavelength lenses are focused at; Education & PEG takes mercury’s yellow pair at 577 and 579 nm, drawn as one line; Posters hydrogen Hδ at 410.2 nm; forums and special events the 467 nm ytterbium-ion clock line; Congress events are a hydrogen lamp: its Hα line is at 656.3 nm, and the discharge glows magenta because Hα mixes with the blue Balmer lines. Plenaries are white light, every stream at once, so they are printed in ink; meals and meetings are neutral greys. Now is marked by the sodium D doublet at 589.0 and 589.6 nm .
